name: Type 2 Diabetes
curability: Not curable, but highly manageable and sometimes reversible into remission with sustained lifestyle change.
conventional_treatment: Metformin or other prescribed glucose-lowering medication
caution: Medication and insulin dosing must be managed by a doctor; exercise can affect blood sugar levels and needs monitoring, especially on insulin.

name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
curability: Not curable, but very controllable through medication and lifestyle change.
conventional_treatment: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, or diuretics as prescribed
caution: Avoid heavy breath-holding strength training (Valsalva maneuver) until blood pressure is well controlled.

name: Coronary Heart Disease
curability: Not curable outright; managed through medication, lifestyle change, and sometimes procedures (stents, bypass surgery).
conventional_treatment: Possible angioplasty/stenting or bypass surgery in severe cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Supervised cardiac rehab walking/cycling, building duration gradually
caution: Exercise for diagnosed heart disease should start under medical supervision, especially after a cardiac event.

name: Osteoarthritis
curability: Not curable; progression can be slowed and symptoms well managed.
conventional_treatment: Pain relief (e.g. acetaminophen or NSAIDs as advised by a doctor)
Joint replacement surgery in advanced cases
caution: Avoid high-impact activity (running, jumping) during flare-ups.

name: Obesity / Weight Management
curability: Manageable and often reversible through sustained lifestyle changes; in some cases medication or surgery is used alongside.
conventional_treatment: Prescribed weight-loss medication in some cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Resistance training to preserve lean mass
Gradual intensity increase (HIIT once base fitness is built)
caution: Increase exercise volume gradually to protect joints carrying extra load.

name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
curability: Highly treatable; many people achieve full symptom remission with therapy, and/or medication, and lifestyle support.
conventional_treatment: SSRIs or other medication as prescribed by a psychiatrist
caution: Exercise supports treatment but does not replace therapy or medication for moderate-to-severe cases.

name: Depression (Major Depressive Disorder)
curability: Highly treatable; many people recover fully or achieve long-term remission with proper care.
conventional_treatment: Antidepressant medication as prescribed by a doctor/psychiatrist
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular aerobic activity (shown to raise BDNF and endorphins)
caution: If there are thoughts of self-harm or suicide, seek immediate professional help rather than relying on exercise alone.

name: Osteoporosis
symptoms: Often silent until a fracture occurs
curability: Not curable, but bone loss can be slowed and fracture risk reduced significantly.
conventional_treatment: Calcium and vitamin D supplementation as advised
Bisphosphonates or other bone-density medication as prescribed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Balance exercises to reduce fall risk
caution: Avoid high-impact jumping or spinal-flexion movements (like full sit-ups) if fracture risk is elevated.

name: Asthma
curability: Not curable, but very well controlled with proper management; many people live symptom-free.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Swimming (humid air is gentler on airways)
caution: Always carry a rescue inhaler during exercise; warm up longer in cold, dry air.

name: COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)
curability: Not curable and generally not reversible, but progression can be slowed and symptoms managed.
caution: Exercise intensity should be built gradually and ideally guided by a pulmonary rehab specialist.

name: Migraine
curability: Not curable, but frequency and severity are often well controlled with trigger management and medication.
conventional_treatment: Triptans or other migraine-specific medication for acute attacks, as prescribed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular, moderate aerobic exercise (can reduce frequency)
caution: Intense exercise can itself trigger a migraine in some people; build up gradually and stay hydrated.

name: GERD (Acid Reflux)
curability: Manageable and often well-controlled with lifestyle change and medication; rarely requires surgery.
conventional_treatment: Antacids or proton pump inhibitors as prescribed
Elevating the head of the bed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Walking after meals (light activity aids digestion)
caution: Avoid exercises with heavy forward bending or intense core compression right after meals.

name: Common Cold / Influenza
curability: Self-limiting — resolves on its own; there is no cure, only supportive care and, for flu, sometimes antiviral medication if caught early.
conventional_treatment: Antiviral medication for flu in some cases if prescribed early
exercise_and_lifestyle: Rest is prioritized over exercise during active illness
Light walking only once fever-free and energy returns
caution: Avoid exercising with a fever or chest symptoms; this can worsen illness or, rarely, affect the heart.

name: Low Back Pain / Sciatica
symptoms: Numbness or tingling down the leg (sciatica)
curability: Most cases resolve or improve significantly with time and conservative treatment; chronic cases are managed long-term.
conventional_treatment: Pain relief as advised by a doctor
Rarely, surgery for severe nerve compression
exercise_and_lifestyle: Gentle stretching (e.g. cat-cow, hip flexor stretches)
caution: Avoid heavy lifting and high-impact activity during acute flare-ups; seek care urgently for loss of bladder/bowel control.

name: Insomnia
curability: Often highly improvable through behavioral changes; chronic cases may need therapy (CBT-I) or short-term medication.
conventional_treatment: Short-term sleep medication only if prescribed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular daytime exercise (not too close to bedtime)
caution: Vigorous exercise too close to bedtime can sometimes delay sleep onset for some people.

name: Hypothyroidism
curability: Not curable, but fully manageable with lifelong thyroid hormone replacement medication.
conventional_treatment: Levothyroxine (thyroid hormone replacement) as prescribed, with regular blood testing
exercise_and_lifestyle: Moderate aerobic exercise as energy allows
caution: Energy levels can be low untreated; exercise intensity should scale with how well the condition is currently controlled.

name: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome)
curability: Not curable, but symptoms are very manageable through lifestyle change and medication.
conventional_treatment: Hormonal birth control or other medication as prescribed
Metformin for insulin resistance in some cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Combination of cardio and strength training (improves insulin sensitivity)
Consistent activity to support weight and hormone balance
caution: Individual response varies widely; track symptoms alongside a doctor rather than self-adjusting treatment.

name: Seasonal Allergies (Allergic Rhinitis)
causes: Pollen, dust, or other airborne allergens
curability: Not curable, but very manageable with medication and allergen avoidance; immunotherapy can reduce sensitivity over years.
conventional_treatment: Allergen immunotherapy (allergy shots) for long-term cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Shower after outdoor activity to remove pollen
Check pollen forecasts before outdoor workouts
caution: Uncontrolled allergy symptoms can worsen asthma if both conditions co-exist.

name: Type 1 Diabetes
curability: Not curable; managed for life with insulin therapy and monitoring.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular moderate exercise with glucose checks before and after
caution: Exercise can cause low blood sugar; insulin adjustments must be guided by a doctor. Very high sugar with vomiting or confusion is an emergency.

name: High Cholesterol (Hyperlipidemia)
symptoms: Fatty deposits around eyes or tendons in severe inherited cases
curability: Not curable but very controllable, often improving substantially with lifestyle change.
conventional_treatment: Statins or other lipid-lowering medication as prescribed
Diet lower in saturated and trans fats
caution: Do not stop prescribed cholesterol medication without medical advice. Report unexplained muscle pain to your doctor.

name: Heart Failure
curability: Not curable; symptoms and progression can be controlled with treatment.
conventional_treatment: ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, diuretics and related medicines as prescribed
Devices or surgery in advanced cases
caution: Exercise should be cleared by a cardiologist. Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or fainting needs urgent care.

name: Atrial Fibrillation
curability: Often manageable long term; some cases can be treated with procedures such as ablation.
conventional_treatment: Blood thinners to reduce stroke risk as prescribed
Cardioversion or catheter ablation in selected cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Moderate regular aerobic exercise once stable
Limit alcohol and caffeine if they trigger episodes
caution: AF raises stroke risk; stroke signs (face droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty) need emergency care immediately.

name: Stroke
symptoms: Arm or leg weakness on one side
curability: A medical emergency; recovery through rehabilitation varies. Prevention of a second stroke is key.
conventional_treatment: Emergency clot-busting drugs or clot removal if treated within hours
Blood pressure, cholesterol and clot-prevention medicines
caution: Call emergency services immediately if you suspect a stroke; every minute matters. Do not wait to see if symptoms pass.

name: Anemia (Iron Deficiency)
curability: Usually curable once the cause is found and iron levels are restored.
conventional_treatment: Iron supplements or iron-rich diet as advised after testing
Treating the underlying cause of blood loss
Vitamin B12 or folate if those are low
exercise_and_lifestyle: Light activity, increasing as energy returns
caution: Do not self-treat with iron long term without testing; find the cause. Severe breathlessness or chest pain needs urgent care.

name: Pneumonia
causes: Bacterial, viral or fungal lung infection
curability: Usually curable; bacterial pneumonia responds to antibiotics prescribed by a doctor.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Gentle walking and deep-breathing exercises during recovery
caution: Difficulty breathing, blue lips, confusion or a very high fever need urgent care, especially in older adults and young children.

name: Tuberculosis (TB)
causes: Mycobacterium tuberculosis spread through the air
curability: Curable with a full course of combination antibiotics taken exactly as prescribed.
conventional_treatment: Multi-drug anti-TB regimen for about 6 months or longer under supervision
caution: Never stop TB treatment early, as this causes drug-resistant TB. See a doctor promptly for a cough lasting over 3 weeks.

name: COVID-19
curability: Usually self-limiting in healthy people; antivirals are available for higher-risk patients.
conventional_treatment: Antiviral treatment for high-risk patients if started early, as prescribed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Return to exercise gradually after recovery
caution: Difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, confusion or blue lips need emergency care.

name: Acute Bronchitis
causes: Usually a viral infection of the airways; sometimes irritants such as smoke
curability: Usually resolves on its own in 1-3 weeks; antibiotics rarely needed.
conventional_treatment: Honey or warm drinks for cough relief
Antibiotics only if bacterial infection is suspected by a doctor
caution: A cough lasting over 3 weeks, coughing blood, or breathing difficulty needs medical review.

name: Sinusitis
curability: Most acute cases clear on their own; chronic cases are manageable.
conventional_treatment: Antibiotics only if bacterial, prescribed by a doctor
exercise_and_lifestyle: Light walking is fine if you feel able
caution: Swelling around the eyes, severe headache, high fever or vision changes need urgent review.

name: Strep Throat / Tonsillitis
causes: Group A Streptococcus bacteria or viruses
curability: Bacterial strep throat is curable with antibiotics prescribed by a doctor; viral cases resolve on their own.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Avoid strenuous exercise until fever has settled
caution: Difficulty breathing, drooling or inability to swallow needs urgent care.

name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
causes: Bacteria, commonly E. coli, entering the urinary tract
curability: Usually curable with a short antibiotic course prescribed by a doctor.
caution: Fever, back or flank pain, vomiting or blood in urine suggests kidney involvement and needs prompt care.

name: Kidney Stones
symptoms: Severe pain in side or back
curability: Small stones often pass on their own; larger stones can be removed with procedures.
conventional_treatment: Medication to help stones pass in some cases
Shockwave lithotripsy or ureteroscopy for large stones
exercise_and_lifestyle: Drink enough fluid for pale urine
caution: Fever with pain, or being unable to pass urine, is an emergency.

name: Chronic Kidney Disease
curability: Not curable; progression can be slowed, and advanced disease is treated with dialysis or transplant.
conventional_treatment: Tight blood pressure and blood sugar control
ACE inhibitors or ARBs as prescribed
Diet guidance on salt, protein and potassium
Dialysis or transplant in end-stage disease
caution: Ask your kidney doctor before taking any new medicine or supplement, as many are cleared by the kidneys.

name: Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu / Food Poisoning)
curability: Usually self-limiting within a few days; rehydration is the main treatment.
conventional_treatment: Antibiotics only for specific bacterial causes, prescribed by a doctor
exercise_and_lifestyle: Avoid exercise until recovered and fully hydrated
caution: Blood in stool, high fever, signs of dehydration (dizziness, very little urine) or symptoms lasting over 3 days need medical care.

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
curability: Not curable but usually well controlled with diet and lifestyle changes.
conventional_treatment: Trigger-food identification, sometimes a low-FODMAP diet with a dietitian
Antispasmodics or other medicines as prescribed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular moderate exercise (walking, yoga) reduces symptoms
caution: Blood in stool, unexplained weight loss or night-time symptoms are not typical of IBS and need medical review.

name: Peptic Ulcer
curability: Usually curable, especially when H. pylori is eradicated.
conventional_treatment: Antibiotics plus acid-reducing medicine for H. pylori as prescribed
caution: Vomiting blood, black tarry stools or sudden severe abdominal pain are emergencies.

name: Constipation
symptoms: Fewer than 3 bowel movements a week
curability: Usually easily managed with diet and lifestyle changes.
conventional_treatment: Osmotic or bulk laxatives as advised
Review of causative medicines with a doctor
exercise_and_lifestyle: Respond promptly to the urge to go
caution: New constipation with blood, weight loss or severe pain, especially over 50, needs medical review.

name: Diarrhea
curability: Usually short-lived and self-limiting; rehydration is the priority.
conventional_treatment: Anti-diarrhoeal medicines only when appropriate and advised
caution: Blood in stool, fever, severe dehydration or diarrhoea lasting more than a few days needs medical care, especially in children and older adults.

name: Viral Hepatitis (A, B, C)
symptoms: Often no symptoms in chronic B and C
causes: Hepatitis viruses spread by contaminated food or water (A) or blood and body fluids (B, C)
curability: Hepatitis A resolves on its own; hepatitis C is now usually curable with antivirals; hepatitis B is controllable.
conventional_treatment: Long-term antiviral therapy for chronic hepatitis B
exercise_and_lifestyle: Safe food and water, safe sex, no sharing needles
caution: Confusion, vomiting blood or severe abdominal swelling need emergency care.

name: Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD)
curability: Often reversible in early stages through weight loss and lifestyle change.
conventional_treatment: Gradual weight loss of 7-10% of body weight
exercise_and_lifestyle: 150+ minutes of aerobic exercise weekly plus resistance training
Cut sugary drinks and refined carbs
caution: Avoid crash diets; rapid weight loss can worsen liver inflammation. See a doctor if there is yellowing of the skin or abdominal swelling.

name: Gallstones
symptoms: Sudden pain in upper right abdomen
curability: Symptomatic gallstones are usually cured by removing the gallbladder; it is not needed to live normally.
caution: Fever with abdominal pain, or jaundice, needs urgent care as it may signal infection or a blocked bile duct.

name: Appendicitis
symptoms: Pain starting near the navel and moving to lower right abdomen
causes: Blockage and infection of the appendix
curability: Curable with surgery to remove the appendix; it is a medical emergency.
conventional_treatment: Fluids and pain relief in hospital
exercise_and_lifestyle: Gradual return to activity after surgery as advised by the surgeon
caution: Seek emergency care right away for suspected appendicitis. A ruptured appendix is life-threatening.

name: Celiac Disease
curability: Not curable but fully controlled by a strict lifelong gluten-free diet.
conventional_treatment: Blood tests and biopsy for diagnosis
Vitamin and mineral supplements if deficient
caution: Do not start a gluten-free diet before testing, as it can hide the diagnosis.

name: Lactose Intolerance
causes: Low levels of the lactase enzyme
curability: Not curable but easily managed by adjusting dairy intake.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Small amounts of dairy are often tolerated
Maintain calcium and vitamin D intake
caution: Persistent symptoms unrelated to dairy should be checked by a doctor.

name: Malaria
causes: Plasmodium parasites spread by Anopheles mosquitoes
curability: Curable with prompt antimalarial treatment prescribed by a doctor.
conventional_treatment: Antimalarial medicines matched to the parasite type
exercise_and_lifestyle: Prevention: mosquito nets, repellents, preventive medicines when travelling
caution: Malaria can become life-threatening within days; seek urgent testing for fever after being in a malaria area.

name: Dengue Fever
causes: Dengue virus spread by Aedes mosquitoes
curability: No specific antiviral; most people recover with supportive care.
conventional_treatment: Paracetamol for fever as directed (avoid aspirin and NSAIDs)
caution: Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums, or drowsiness after fever settles are warning signs needing immediate hospital care.

name: Typhoid Fever
causes: Salmonella Typhi from contaminated food or water
curability: Curable with antibiotics prescribed by a doctor.
caution: Complete the whole antibiotic course. Severe abdominal pain or bleeding needs emergency care.

name: Chickenpox
curability: Usually mild and self-limiting; vaccination prevents it.
conventional_treatment: Calamine or cooling lotions for itch
Antivirals for high-risk patients if prescribed early
exercise_and_lifestyle: Stay home until all blisters have crusted
Avoid contact with pregnant women and newborns
caution: Avoid aspirin in children. Seek care for breathing difficulty, confusion or spreading redness.

name: Measles
curability: No specific cure; most recover with supportive care, and the MMR vaccine prevents it.
conventional_treatment: Vitamin A in some settings under medical advice
exercise_and_lifestyle: Ensure MMR vaccination is up to date
caution: Complications like pneumonia and encephalitis can be serious; seek care for breathing trouble, seizures or drowsiness.

name: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye)
curability: Usually resolves on its own; bacterial cases may need antibiotic drops from a doctor.
conventional_treatment: Clean discharge with a clean, damp cloth
Antibiotic drops if bacterial, as prescribed
caution: Eye pain, reduced vision or sensitivity to light needs urgent eye assessment.

name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
curability: Not curable but well controlled; many children outgrow it.
conventional_treatment: Topical corticosteroids or other creams as prescribed
caution: Weeping, crusted or painful skin may be infected and needs a doctor.

name: Psoriasis
curability: Not curable but usually well controlled with treatment.
conventional_treatment: Systemic or biologic medicines for moderate to severe cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular exercise and weight control help
caution: Joint pain and stiffness with psoriasis should be assessed for psoriatic arthritis.

name: Acne
curability: Highly treatable; most cases can be cleared or greatly improved.
conventional_treatment: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide or antibiotics
Oral antibiotics or hormonal treatment for moderate cases
Isotretinoin for severe acne under specialist care
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular exercise, then wash after sweating
caution: Severe or scarring acne should be treated early by a doctor or dermatologist.

name: Fungal Skin Infection (Ringworm / Athlete's Foot)
causes: Dermatophyte fungi thriving in warm, moist areas
curability: Curable with antifungal treatment.
conventional_treatment: Oral antifungals for widespread or nail infections as prescribed
caution: Continue treatment for the full recommended period even after the rash fades.

name: Scabies
symptoms: Tiny burrows or bumps between fingers
causes: Sarcoptes scabiei mites spread by close contact
curability: Curable with prescribed anti-scabies treatment for the patient and close contacts.
conventional_treatment: Treat all household contacts at the same time
Wash bedding and clothes in hot water
exercise_and_lifestyle: Itching may continue for weeks after treatment
caution: See a doctor rather than guessing, since other skin conditions can look similar.

name: Urticaria (Hives)
curability: Acute hives usually settle in days to weeks; chronic hives are manageable.
caution: Swelling of the tongue or throat, wheeze or dizziness is an emergency (possible anaphylaxis).

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
curability: Not curable, but early treatment can produce remission and prevent joint damage.
conventional_treatment: Disease-modifying drugs (DMARDs) and biologics as prescribed by a rheumatologist
exercise_and_lifestyle: Low-impact exercise like swimming and cycling
caution: Early specialist treatment matters; joint damage can be permanent if untreated.

name: Gout
symptoms: Sudden severe joint pain, often the big toe
causes: High uric acid forming crystals in joints
Diet high in purines and alcohol
curability: Not curable but well controlled with treatment and lifestyle change.
conventional_treatment: Anti-inflammatory medicines or colchicine for flares as prescribed
Reduced alcohol, sugary drinks and red meat
caution: Rest the joint during a flare; a hot swollen joint with fever needs urgent assessment to exclude infection.

name: Fibromyalgia
causes: Altered pain processing in the nervous system
curability: Not curable but symptoms can improve significantly with a combined approach.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Start with gentle walking, swimming or yoga and increase slowly
caution: Overdoing exercise early can cause flare-ups; build up gradually.

name: Tendinitis / Tennis Elbow
symptoms: Pain near a joint that worsens with use
curability: Usually heals with rest and rehabilitation over weeks to months.
conventional_treatment: Injections or surgery in stubborn cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Eccentric strengthening exercises guided by a physio
caution: Sudden loss of function or a popping sensation may indicate a tendon tear and needs assessment.

name: Plantar Fasciitis
symptoms: Sharp heel pain, worst with first steps in the morning
curability: Usually improves within months with consistent self-care.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Low-impact exercise like swimming or cycling while healing
caution: Persistent pain beyond a few months needs assessment.

name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
symptoms: Numbness or tingling in thumb and fingers
causes: Compression of the median nerve at the wrist
curability: Often improves with conservative care; surgery can cure persistent cases.
conventional_treatment: Surgical release if severe or persistent
caution: Constant numbness or muscle wasting at the thumb base needs prompt assessment.

name: Ankle Sprain
symptoms: Pain and swelling around the ankle
causes: Sudden twisting of the ankle stretching or tearing ligaments
curability: Usually heals fully with proper care in a few weeks.
conventional_treatment: Rest, ice, compression and elevation early on
exercise_and_lifestyle: Gentle range-of-motion then balance and strengthening exercises
caution: Inability to walk four steps or bone tenderness may indicate a fracture and needs an X-ray.

name: Tension Headache
symptoms: Dull band-like pressure around the head
curability: Very common and manageable; usually not serious.
caution: Sudden thunderclap headache, headache with fever and stiff neck, or after head injury needs emergency care.

name: Epilepsy
curability: Not curable in most cases but controlled with medication in about 70% of people.
conventional_treatment: Anti-seizure medicines taken regularly as prescribed
Surgery or nerve stimulation in drug-resistant cases
exercise_and_lifestyle: Avoid alcohol excess and sleep deprivation
caution: Call emergency services if a seizure lasts over 5 minutes or repeats without recovery. Take precautions around water and heights.

name: Parkinson's Disease
curability: Not curable; symptoms are managed with medication and therapy for many years.
conventional_treatment: Levodopa and other dopamine-related medicines as prescribed
Deep brain stimulation in selected patients
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular exercise (walking, cycling, tai chi, boxing-style programmes) improves mobility and balance
caution: Regular neurologist review is important as medication needs change over time.

name: Alzheimer's Disease / Dementia
curability: Not curable; some medicines and care approaches can ease symptoms and support quality of life.
conventional_treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors or other medicines as prescribed
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular physical activity supports brain health
caution: Sudden confusion can signal infection or stroke and needs urgent evaluation.

name: Vertigo (BPPV)
causes: Displaced crystals in the inner ear (BPPV)
curability: BPPV is often cured in one or two sessions of a repositioning manoeuvre (Epley).
conventional_treatment: Epley or other repositioning manoeuvres by a trained clinician
exercise_and_lifestyle: Avoid sudden head movements during episodes
caution: Vertigo with double vision, weakness, slurred speech or severe headache needs emergency evaluation for stroke.

name: Bipolar Disorder
symptoms: Episodes of elevated or irritable mood
curability: Not curable but usually well controlled with long-term treatment.
conventional_treatment: Mood stabilisers and other medicines as prescribed by a psychiatrist
caution: Do not stop medication suddenly. Thoughts of self-harm need immediate professional help.

name: ADHD (Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder)
curability: Not curable but symptoms are very manageable with the right support.
conventional_treatment: Stimulant or non-stimulant medication as prescribed by a specialist
caution: Diagnosis and medication should be handled by a qualified clinician.

name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
curability: Highly treatable; many people recover substantially with trauma-focused therapy.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular exercise and yoga can reduce arousal
caution: If you are having thoughts of self-harm, seek immediate help from a crisis service or emergency care.

name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
curability: Not usually curable but very effectively treated; weight loss can resolve mild cases.
caution: Untreated sleep apnea raises risk of high blood pressure, heart disease and accidents from drowsiness.

name: Hyperthyroidism
curability: Usually curable or well controlled with treatment.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Avoid strenuous exercise until thyroid levels are controlled
caution: Chest pain, very fast heartbeat or confusion needs urgent care.

name: Menstrual Cramps (Dysmenorrhea)
symptoms: Cramping lower abdominal pain before or during periods
causes: Endometriosis or fibroids in secondary cases
curability: Usually manageable; underlying causes can be treated if found.
caution: Severe pain that disrupts daily life, or pain that is getting worse, should be assessed by a doctor.

name: Endometriosis
causes: Tissue similar to womb lining growing outside the uterus
curability: Not curable but symptoms can be controlled; surgery can remove lesions.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Regular low-impact exercise and pelvic-floor physiotherapy
caution: Diagnosis is often delayed; persistent pelvic pain deserves specialist review.

name: Enlarged Prostate (BPH)
causes: Age-related prostate growth and hormonal changes
curability: Not curable but treatable; symptoms can be relieved with medication or surgery.
conventional_treatment: Alpha blockers and 5-alpha reductase inhibitors as prescribed
caution: Being unable to urinate, blood in urine or fever with urinary symptoms needs urgent care.

name: Menopause Symptoms
causes: Natural fall in oestrogen with ageing
curability: A natural stage of life; symptoms are manageable rather than a disease to cure.
conventional_treatment: Hormone replacement therapy for suitable patients, discussed with a doctor
exercise_and_lifestyle: Weight-bearing and resistance exercise protect bones
caution: Bleeding after menopause should always be checked by a doctor. Bone health monitoring is important.

name: Vitamin D Deficiency
curability: Easily corrected with supplementation and sensible sun exposure guided by testing.
conventional_treatment: Foods such as oily fish and fortified products
caution: Very high supplement doses can be harmful; follow medical guidance.

name: Dehydration
curability: Mild dehydration is quickly reversed by drinking fluids; severe cases need medical care.
conventional_treatment: Water or oral rehydration solution in small frequent sips
Treat the cause such as vomiting or diarrhoea
exercise_and_lifestyle: Drink regularly through the day and around exercise
Avoid strenuous exercise in heat until rehydrated
caution: Confusion, fainting, rapid heartbeat, or inability to keep fluids down needs urgent medical care, particularly in children and older adults.

name: Dental Cavities & Gum Disease
curability: Cavities are treated with fillings; early gum disease is reversible with good oral care.
exercise_and_lifestyle: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
caution: Facial swelling, fever or severe pain suggests an abscess and needs prompt dental or medical care.
